scope: Corollary 8.2 (Binary Morse spectral consequence) of the manuscript “Asymptotically minimal maxima of real Littlewood polynomials” (preprints/Asymptotically-minimal-maxima-of-real-Littlewood-polynomials-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 076 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3f6f94e6343c03b7), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a binary Morse shift (X, S) with a unique S-invariant Borel probability measure µ for which the Koopman operator USg = g ◦ S on L2(X, µ) has simple spectrum. For the zero-coordinate function f(x) = x(0), let σf be the spectral measure characterized by c σf (n) := Z T e(nt) dσf (t) = Z X f(x)f(Sn x) dµ(x) (n ∈ Z). Then dσf = h dt for some h ∈ L2(T) with h ≥ 0 almost everywhere and R T h dt = 1. In particular, the absolutely continuous spectral component is nonzero.
